Water and Waste: A History of Reluctant Policymaking in U.S. Cities
abstract: U.S. cities experienced a sanitary revolution during the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The abandonment of cesspools, privy vaults for waste containment and cisterns, pumps, and shallow wells for water delivery brought about a large increase in living standards. While the gains are impressive, investments were often made reluctantly. Scientific advances clarifying the origins of waterborne illness improved, and filtration plants and universal access to water and safe sewerage offered a solution. Yet few cities made those investments. Only with chlorination, a low-cost purification solution, did rapid adoption occur. These delays came at a large human cost.
abstract_zh: 19世纪和20世纪初，美国城市经历了一场卫生革命。废弃化粪池、用于收集废物的厕所粪坑和蓄水池，以及用于供水的水泵和浅井，使生活水平大幅提高。尽管成就令人瞩目，但这些投资往往是勉强进行的。随着阐明水源性疾病起源的科学进步，过滤厂以及通用的供水和安全下水道系统提供了解决方案。然而，很少有城市进行这些投资。直到氯化消毒这一低成本净化方案出现，才实现了快速普及。这些延误付出了巨大的人力代价。

Segregation and the Initial Provision of Water in the United States
abstract: US cities invested heavily in water and sewer infrastructure throughout the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. These investments improved public health and quality of life by helping US cities control typhoid fever and other waterborne diseases. We show that segregated cities invested in water infrastructure earlier but were slower to reach universal access and slower to eliminate typhoid fever. We develop a theoretical model that illustrates how segregation, by facilitating the exclusion of Black households from water and sewer systems, explains these seemingly paradoxical findings.
abstract_zh: 19世纪末至20世纪初，美国城市在供水和下水道基础设施方面投入巨大。这些投资通过帮助美国城市控制伤寒及其他水源性疾病，改善了公共健康和生活质量。我们发现，实行种族隔离的城市更早投资于供水基础设施，但在实现普遍覆盖和消除伤寒方面进展较慢。我们构建了一个理论模型，阐明种族隔离如何通过排斥黑人家庭获得供水和下水道系统，从而解释了这些看似矛盾的发现。

title: The 1918 Influenza Pandemic and its Lessons for COVID-19
Water Infrastructure and Health in U.S. Cities
abstract: Between 1900 and 1930 typhoid fever and other waterborne diseases were largely eradicated from U.S. cities. This achievement required a mix of technological, scientific, economic, and bureaucratic innovations. This article examines how the interaction of those forces influenced water and sanitary infrastructure provision during the 19th and early 20th centuries. I show the sharp link between infrastructure investments and declines in waterborne disease and discuss how that relationship informs the methodological approaches one should use to assess the impact of sanitary investments on urban development. Finally, I review the literature on the social returns to eliminating the threat of waterborne disease. The evidence suggests the benefits of infrastructure investment far exceeded the costs.
abstract_zh: 1900年至1930年间，伤寒及其他水源性疾病在美国城市中基本被消灭。这一成就需要技术、科学、经济和官僚层面的多重创新相互配合。本文考察了这些力量的相互作用如何影响19世纪和20世纪初的供水与卫生基础设施供给。我展示了基础设施投资与水源性疾病下降之间的紧密联系，并讨论了这一关系如何为评估卫生投资对城市发展影响的方法论途径提供参考。最后，我回顾了关于消除水源性疾病威胁的社会收益的文献。证据表明，基础设施投资的收益远超其成本。

Coal Smoke and Mortality in an Early Industrial Economy
abstract: Air pollution was severe in the nineteenth century, yet its health consequences are often overlooked due to a lack of pollution data. We offer a new approach for inferring local coal use levels based on local industrial structure and industry‐specific coal use intensity. This allows us to provide the first estimates of the mortality effects of British industrial coal use in 1851–60. Exploiting wind patterns for identification, we find that a one standard deviation increase in coal use raised infant mortality by 6–8% and that industrial coal use explains roughly one‐third of the urban mortality penalty observed during this period.
abstract_zh: 19世纪的空气污染十分严重，但由于缺乏污染数据，其健康后果常常被忽视。我们提出了一种新方法，基于当地工业结构和分行业用煤强度来推断当地用煤水平。这使我们首次估计出1851—60年英国工业用煤对死亡率的影响。利用风向进行识别，我们发现煤炭用量每增加一个标准差，婴儿死亡率上升6%—8%；并且，工业用煤可解释该时期城市死亡率劣势的约三分之一。

title: Gridlock: Ethnic Diversity in Government and the Provision of Public Goods
Business as Usual: Politicians with Business Experience, Government Finances, and Policy Outcomes
Typhoid Fever, Water Quality, and Human Capital Formation
abstract: New water purification technologies led to large mortality declines by helping eliminate typhoid fever and other waterborne diseases. We examine how this affected human capital formation using early-life typhoid fatality rates to proxy for water quality. We merge city-level data to individuals linked between the 1900 and 1940 Censuses. Eliminating early-life exposure to typhoid fever increased later-life earnings by one percent and educational attainment by one month. Instrumenting for typhoid fever using typhoid rates from cities that lie upstream produces results nine times larger. The increase in earnings from eliminating typhoid fever more than offset the cost of elimination.
abstract_zh: 新的水净化技术通过帮助消除伤寒及其他水源性疾病，大幅降低了死亡率。我们利用早期生活中的伤寒致死率作为水质的代理变量，考察了这一变化如何影响人力资本形成。我们将城市层面的数据与1900年和1940年人口普查之间可追踪的个人数据进行了匹配。消除生命早期接触伤寒的风险，使成年后的收入提高了1%，受教育程度提高了一个月。以位于上游城市的伤寒率作为工具变量对伤寒进行工具化处理，得到的结果是前者的九倍。消除伤寒所带来的收入增加，足以抵消消除伤寒的成本。
